title: Developer Docs: Authoring Gateway and Offline Release Playbook
author: Priya Nair
body:
Overview:

This playbook defines the Authoring Gateway pattern for Redwood developer docs: a lightweight pipeline and set of conventions that let contributors edit SDK guides, API examples, and docs-site snippets offline, validate them locally, and release changes through a staged rollout with automated checks and canonical fixes for top support issues. The goal is to reduce merge/revert cycles, shrink hotfix blast radius, and standardize how doc fixes for common support problems are produced and released.

Scope:
- Applies to: SDK guides, API examples, quickstarts, snippet libraries, and docs-site content under eng-developer-experience.
- Excludes: private customer-runbooks in customer repos, legal/policy documents (use policies-and-process).

Why this exists:
- Many fixes originate in support tickets and require a fast, low-risk path to publish corrected snippets and guidance.
- Offline authoring reduces friction for contributors in restricted networks or with flaky CI.
- A repeatable release orchestration (canary -> staging -> global) reduces regressions and enables targeted rollbacks.

Roles & Ownership:
- Documentation author (author-team): creates/edits content, runs local checks, opens PR.
- Docs oncall (rotation): triages release failures and coordinates emergency hotfixes.
- DX Release Engineer (owner_team: engineering): approves staged rollouts, manages release pipeline.
- Reviewers: subject-matter experts for SDK or API area (listed on PR).

Authoring Gateway pattern (step-by-step):
1) Local authoring and metadata:
   - Create a branch named docs/<area>/<short-desc> (e.g., docs/sdk/streaming-fallback-fix).
   - Update page front-matter: title, short-description, affected-versions (comma list), and labels. Example front-matter block used in our site generator:

```yaml
title: "Streaming fallback: client resilience patterns"
affected_versions: "sdk-1.x, sdk-2.0"
labels: ["sdk","resilience","example"]
```

2) Preflight checks (local):
   - Run local validator: tools/docs-validate --spell --links --snippet-check.
   - Run SDK snippet runner (ensures example calls compile/run): tools/snippet-runner --path examples/sdk --timeout 20s.
   - Ensure telemetry markers are present for any canonical fix: <!-- telemetry:ticket=IN-12345 -->

3) PR: Create PR against docs branch (topic -> staging-docs). In PR description include: problem statement, reproducer steps (if from support), tests ran, and rollback notes. Use template: docs/pr-templates/reproduction-and-fix.md.

4) Automated checks in CI:
   - Lint & style checks (docs-lint).
   - Snippet-runner (CI will run longer timeouts and matrix for languages).
   - Link-checker for external references.
   - Telemetry annotation check to ensure support tickets are referenced.

5) Staged release gating (after PR merge):
   - Canary window (1 hour): content published to canary URL under dev.docs.redwood.ai/canary. Observability: docs-publish-trace, page load metric, and snippet success rate.
   - Staging window (24 hours): if canary passes, content promoted to staging (internal-only). Product/Support review occurs here.
   - Global publish: timed rollout with low-traffic release first, then full propagation across CDN.

Release orchestration commands (CLI):
- Publish to canary: docs-publish --target=canary --commit=HEAD
- Promote to staging: docs-publish --target=staging --from=canary
- Promote to global: docs-publish --target=global --from=staging --schedule="2026-02-10T03:00Z"
- Rollback to previous version: docs-publish --target=global --rollback=1

Operational checks & SLOs for doc releases:
- Canary acceptance SLO: snippet execution success >= 99% and fewer than 3 new 404s in canary window.
- Staging acceptance SLO: no critical feedback from support/product within 24h.
- Global release SLA: publish propagation complete within 30 minutes once promoted to global.

Canonical fixes for top support issue patterns:
The table below lists common issues, canonical fix guidance, and testing checklist. Authors should reference these when authoring fixes.

Issue | Canonical Fix Pattern | Local Tests
------|------------------------|------------
SDK authentication errors (expired key examples) | Update example to use ephemeral API key flow and include token refresh snippet; add note about common permission decays. | snippet-runner auth-test, jwt-validate
Streaming resumption failures | Add idempotency key example and stream-resume header sample; show both client and server retry logic. | snippet-runner stream-resume --simulate-drop
Example input/output mismatch with model changes | Add model-version pin in snippet and recommended fallback policy; include sample regression test. | snippet-runner with model-mock and golden-output diff
Rate-limit handling confusion | Show exponential backoff sample + best-effort queuing and SDK helper usage; include server-side quotas note. | snippet-runner rate-limit --rps 50

(Authors: add a telemetry comment linking the original ticket id to any canonical fix.)

Standard templates and snippets to reuse:
- Quickstart skeleton (quickstart-skeleton.md): one-page layout with TL;DR, step-by-step, minimal runnable snippet.
- API example pattern (api-example-template.md): problem statement, request/response JSON, SDK example in 3 languages, validation script.
- Hotfix playbook template (hotfix-release.md): emergency PR checklist, rollback steps, and comms template for support and product.

SDK example (three-line JS generation snippet used in many pages):
```javascript
import Redwood from '@redwood/inference-js';
const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.RW_API_KEY });
const resp = await client.generate({ model: 'redwood-1-small', prompt: 'Summarize the text:' });
console.log(resp.output[0].text);
```

Diagnostics & observability for doc releases:
- Release traces: docs-publish-trace (attach commit SHA and page list).
- Snippet telemetry: snippet-runner emits success/failure events to docs-telemetry; tags: page, language, release-target.
- Errors: pages generating new 500s or failing snippet-runner should trigger docs-oncall with priority P2.

Emergency hotfix flow (when to use):
1) Problem detected in global release that causes client breakage or mass confusion (>=10 support tickets in 1h).
2) Open an emergency hotfix PR using branch emergency/<short-desc>.
3) Docs Release Engineer approves, CI runs fast checks (lint + minimal snippet-runner).
4) Publish directly to global with flag --emergency and notify support + status-page owners.
5) After hotfix, follow normal postmortem and update canonical-fix table.

Checklist before merging a doc fix (must be present in PR description):
- Problem statement and reproducer steps (if from support).
- Local validation logs attached (validator output and snippet-runner logs).
- Reviewer sign-off from area SME.
- Rollback note: what to revert if publish shows regressions.
- Telemetry ticket link.

Appendix: Example PR description template (copy into PR body):

Problem:
- Short description of the user-facing problem.
- Support ticket: IN-12345 (link).

Fix implemented:
- Files changed and short summary.
- Snippets added/updated.

Validation:
- Local: tools/docs-validate --links -> OK
- Snippets: tools/snippet-runner -> OK

Risk and rollback plan:
- Estimated impact: low/medium/high
- Rollback command: docs-publish --target=global --rollback=1

Related pages and resources:
- docs-site contributor guide: /confluence/eng-developer-experience/docs-site/docs-site-contributor-onboarding-and-lint-pipeline-2026
- Snippet runner docs: /tools/snippet-runner/README
- PR templates: /confluence/eng-developer-experience/docs-site/pr-templates

Owners and contact points:
- DX Release Engineer: dx-release@redwood.com
- Docs oncall rotation: docs-oncall@redwood.com
- Support triage for doc-related tickets: docs-support@redwood.com
